correctness.rationale: Lucas factorization of central trinomial coefficients gives T_n modulo 5 as the product of digit weights (1,1,3,2,4), all nonzero. Using the exact identity 2M_n=3T_n+2T_(n+1)-T_(n+2), the two consecutive Motzkin residues for n=5q+d equal U(q)(f_d(R(q)),g_d(R(q))) for twenty explicit d,R cells. Direct independent computation reproduced all twenty cells, the 80-point push-forward matrix and absence of (0,0), and matched direct Motzkin values for 700 n. For an aligned q interval of length 5^r the carry-run length h<r has one admissible prior digit for each ratio R; products of free digit weights give each U-value 5^(r-h-1)/4+O(1). Summing h yields the 5^r/16+O(r+1) joint equidistribution; h=r costs at most one endpoint. Disjoint base-five aligned blocks for arbitrary Q add O((log Q)^2) discrepancy. Hence each of the 25 pair frequencies has the claimed rational coefficient /80 for every cutoff N; the impossible (0,0) follows exactly and is not an asymptotic inference.

evidence: Kohen, Uniform recurrence in the Motzkin numbers and related sequences mod p (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00149): Kohen's recurrence framework is a prior antecedent, not a theorem giving the 80-case push-forward count.

Rampersad and Shallit, Congruence properties of combinatorial sequences via Walnut and the Rowland–Yassawi–Zeilberger automaton (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06244): Recognizing a regular language does not alone fix its natural density/discrepancy without transition analysis.

Burns, Structure and asymptotics for Motzkin numbers modulo small primes using automata (https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08146): A one-variable marginal does not determine a joint neighboring distribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The automaton frameworks could algorithmically derive pair counts, but none of the inspected general recurrence/automaticity theorems directly implies a specific 25-cell density with O(log^2 N) all-cutoff bound without additional state and carry distribution evaluation.
